subject.title: fix(irc): disconnect on oversized inbound lines

question: Should an oversized inbound IRC record trigger automatic account recovery, or is a persistent fail-closed disconnect until operator action the intended contract?
rationale: Both behaviors are defensible security postures, but the low-level client cannot choose the channel availability and operator-recovery policy on its own.

options.title: Add lifecycle recovery proof
options.body: Wire or verify post-ready client termination through the IRC gateway lifecycle so the account becomes failed and reconnects with bounded backoff.

options.title: Accept fail-closed disconnect
options.body: Merge the strict disconnect behavior and explicitly own the possibility that an affected IRC account requires operator restart after one oversized server record.

options.title: Use a larger safety ceiling
options.body: Pause this exact protocol cap and instead bound retained input at a higher defensive ceiling if compatibility with non-compliant servers is preferred.

recommendation.title: Add lifecycle recovery proof
recommendation.body: Wire or verify post-ready client termination through the IRC gateway lifecycle so the account becomes failed and reconnects with bounded backoff.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository identifies this person as the IRC area owner, making them the best available owner for the recovery-policy choice.
